standard_deduction_single.note: 2025 figure carried forward; NCDOR had not published a separate 2026 amount at time of research.

senior_addl_deduction_per_person.note: No additional NC standard deduction for age 65+; NC has not adopted the federal OBBBA senior deduction.

social_security.note: Fully exempt regardless of income level; taxpayers deduct any federally-taxed SS benefits on Form D-400 Schedule S.

retirement_income.note: Private pensions, 401(k)/403(b), and traditional IRA distributions are fully taxable as ordinary income -- no exemption. The Bailey settlement only exempts government pensions (federal/state/local) where the retiree had 5+ years of creditable service and was vested as of Aug 12, 1989 -- not modeled here since this app's IRA/401(k) income is private-style, not a grandfathered government pension.

senior_tax_credits.note: None found -- NC offers no additional income-tax deduction, exemption, or credit tied specifically to age 65+.

effective_rate_pct.unit: % of home value/year, statewide avg effective rate
effective_rate_pct.note: Median bill ~$1,502/yr on a $235,312 home; NC ranks #33 of 50 states (2024 Census ACS data).

property_tax.relief_programs_note: Elderly/Disabled Homestead Exclusion: age 65+ (or totally/permanently disabled), owned and occupied as permanent residence as of Jan 1, 2025 income limit $38,800 (adjusted annually via SS COLA) -- excludes the greater of $25,000 or 50% of appraised value. Circuit Breaker Tax Deferment: owned/occupied home 5+ years, caps property tax at 4% of income (income <= $38,800) or 5% of income (income <= $58,200), with the excess deferred as a lien (not forgiven). Both are income-tested well below typical retirement-planning income and not applied to the estimate below.
